subject: POC trial: model selection, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@acmehealth.com>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: model selection, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Sofia / Carlos —

Thanks again for a great discovery call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can get the right stakeholders aligned: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Goal: Validate a clinical triage assistant that can summarize intake notes, classify urgency, and generate patient-facing explanations in English + Spanish.
- Volume for trial: ~10k interactions over a 30-day pilot; peak throughput ~25 req/s.
- Constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data concerns, prefer US region hosting, and a hard latency expectation for production (p95 < 250ms once optimized).

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Success criteria
   - Accuracy: >= 90% match against your clinical rubric on a 200-sample eval set (we'll provide evaluation harness)
   - Latency: p95 < 250ms on the Dedicated profile (after autoscaling)
   - Cost: keep inference spend within the budget we discussed (TBD in MAP)
   - Stability: no more than 2% error rate (timeouts/500s) over a 7-day steady-state window

2) Model selection for trial
   - Primary model: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized FP16 / 4-bit) — good balance of instruction-following, cost, and multilingual capability.
   - Fallback model: Mistral-Instruct-7B (lower cost, faster for short-form classification) — route flows here for low-latency classification tasks and when prefix cache hits are high.
   - Edge case: For fallback on hallucination-prone prompts we can route to a larger instruct model (Falcon-40B-Instruct) on-demand (burst capacity) — this will be optional and metered separately.

3) Multilingual approach
   - Use the primary model for both English and Spanish. For Spanish, we'll include an eval set and a small fine-tune / prompt augmentation for regional phrasing if needed.

4) Ownership & roles
   - Redwood: Aditya (SE) will own model config, benchmarking, and infra tuning. Monica (CS) will own onboarding and runbooks.
   - Acme: Sofia will own clinical rubric and evaluation reviewers; Carlos will own procurement/comms.

5) Timeline (proposed)
   - Kickoff: Jul 15
   - Eval dataset & MAP deliverable: Jul 18
   - Initial model baseline + latency bench: Jul 22
   - 30-day trial window: Jul 25 - Aug 24

Next steps:
- I'll drop the MAP + SOW stub and our evaluation prompt set to the Drive link and DocuSign for signature.
- Aditya: can you attach the initial eval prompt set and a short benchmarking checklist?

Thanks — I'll coordinate the kickoff calendar invite once we confirm Jul 15 works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: evaluation_prompt_set_v1.csv (CSV, 35KB)

Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. Jul 15 for kickoff should work, I'm checking with our clinical reviewers for availability. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Multilingual: Spanish coverage is a hard requirement — some of our intake notes include regional idioms and medical shorthand. If you recommend Llama-2-13B-chat for Spanish, will you also include guidance on prompt templates or a small few-shot tuning pass?

2) Fallbacks & hallucination: For clinical content we need a guaranteed fallback workflow (e.g., escalate to human review or a safe-respond template) if confidence is low. Can you surface model confidence or a heuristic we can rely on?

3) Data residency: We need the trial to run in a US region and would like to see what logs/retention options are available for SOC2 evidence.

If you can send the MAP and the evaluation prompt set, I'll start rounding up our reviewers.

Thanks,
Sofia
Director of Clinical Ops, Acme Health
s.lopez@acmehealth.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Lopez <s.lopez@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Sofia —

Great questions. Quick technical notes and recommendations for the POC configuration: 

1) Spanish performance & prompt guidance
   - Llama-2-13B-chat performs well on general Spanish; for clinical shorthand we recommend: (a) 4-6 shot prompting using
      your clinical rubric examples, (b) a post-process canonicalization pass (simple rules to normalize abbreviations), and
      (c) an evaluation subset focused on regional idioms. We'll provide a short prompt-template doc.

2) Confidence & hallucination mitigation
   - We recommend a combined heuristic: token-level entropy + model logit gap for top tokens + a rules-based check against a medical-terms whitelist.
   - When heuristic < threshold, route the item to: 1) a safe-respond template (do not hallucinate), and 2) flag for human review via your ticketing system.

3) Model selection details
   - Baseline: Llama-2-13B-chat (4-bit quant). We'll run a latency bench with prefix caching (cache warm) and measure cold/warm p95.
   - Fallback: Mistral-Instruct-7B for fast classification and short answers. For high-certainty escalation we can optionally route to Falcon-40B-Instruct for verification; we'd keep that as an opt-in burst due to cost.

4) Infra & logging
   - We will run the POC in Redwood Dedicated (US region) per your request. Logs: request/response logs are available with configurable retention; SOC2 artefacts (audit logs) available on request.

Attachments: I've attached a short benchmarking checklist and the initial eval prompt set (CSV).

I'll coordinate with Monica on runbooks and on-call routing for the trial.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

Please review the MAP and SOW and mark any items you want adjusted before the kickoff. If procurement needs alternate contract language I'm happy to loop in legal but wanted to surface any redlines early.

I'll send a calendar invite for Jul 15 EOD PT — provisional until you confirm.

Best,
Marissa
